children: a lithium exploration license in Germany, in the Berlin Area.

"The license was secured at minimal cost and requires minimal capital commitment over the first few years. It represents optionality rather than a change in strategy," said E3 Lithium’s CEO Chris Doornbos.

The exclusive rights include the exploration and development of lithium and other minerals contained in the formation fluids within an unexplored 754 km² area near Berlin for a 5-year term. The target formation in this area is the Upper Rotliegend sandstones, which are known to be lithium bearing and contain significant resources and relatively high lithium grades by other developers in this region of Germany.

The company plans to source partners and funding within Europe for the development of this project by forming a German entity which is expected to hire its own management team and leverage expertise from E3’s technical team. This license leverages the company’s technical expertise in lithium extraction to create additional long-term shareholder value.
However, Alberta will remain as the company’s core focus, given the advanced development of the Clearwater Project.

title: E3 Lithium awarded exploration license in Germany
